# External slice: XQuAD (English, German, Greek)

A fixed slice of a public benchmark, run separately from the synthetic suites with `make eval-external` (about 10 minutes; opt-in, not part of `make eval` or CI). It is reported, never gated, and no threshold, prompt or setting was changed after seeing it.

- **Source:** XQuAD, Artetxe, Ruder and Yogatama, "On the Cross-lingual Transferability of Monolingual Representations" (2019), <https://github.com/google-deepmind/xquad> at commit `7d30520c717524000f0d9d2f9c10a069acd9d285`. 240 Wikipedia paragraphs and 1,190 questions from the SQuAD v1.1 development set, professionally translated; parallel across languages.
- **Licence:** CC BY-SA 4.0 ([LICENSE-CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt](LICENSE-CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt)). `corpus/` and `cases.json` are adapted material (paragraph texts split into files, questions and answer spans reformatted) and stay under that licence; the rest of the repository is Apache-2.0. Paragraphs and questions come from SQuAD v1.1 (CC BY-SA 4.0).
- **Languages:** English, German and Greek only. XQuAD has no French, so French is not covered here.
- **Provenance pipeline:** `python eval/build_external_corpus.py` downloads the three source files from the pinned commit, checks their SHA-256 (listed in the script), applies the selection rule below and writes `corpus/` and `cases.json`. The source files are not committed.
- **Selection rule (fixed before any run):** articles in file order, minus the three about individual people (Nikola Tesla, Martin Luther, Genghis Khan); the first 2 paragraphs of each remaining article; the first 2 questions of each paragraph. That gives 90 paragraphs and 179 questions, run in five question-language to document-language pairs: en to en, de to de, el to el, and de to en, el to en (cross-lingual). 895 cases in all. The text is public encyclopedic content that names public figures incidentally; it holds no data about private individuals.
- **Metric definitions:** `answered` = did not abstain. `gold_source_cited` = the gold paragraph is among the answer's citations. `all_keywords_in_answer` = the gold answer span appears (case-insensitively) in the answer text. `entailed` = every answer sentence passed the NLI grounding check (of answered cases only). `passed` = gold source cited and answer span present and not abstained. Answers come from the deterministic extractive answerer, so a missing span with the right paragraph cited points at the answerer, not retrieval (not inspected case by case).

Results and reading: [eval/README.md](../README.md#external-slice-xquad).
